sense: on behalf of, in favour of

terms.gloss: for, on behalf of, in defence of
evidence: Hor. C. 3.2.13: dulce et decōrum est prō patriā morī
Ter. Ph. 475: haud cessāvit prō tē ēnītī
terms.comment: For the person or cause one works, speaks or fights for. The same word gives “instead of” and “in return for” (see instead; in exchange for).

terms.gloss: for (the person who gains by it)
terms.grammar: construction: the person in the dative, with no preposition
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.12: nec sibi sōlī, sed conjugī, līberīs
terms.comment: The person something is done for, to his good or harm, stands in the dative.

terms.gloss: on behalf of, in the name of
terms.grammar: the ablative of nōmen, with a genitive or a possessive (meō, tuō nōmine)
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.16.16: Antōniō tuō nōmine grātiās ēgī
terms.comment: When one acts as someone’s representative; see represent.

phrases.latin: dulce et decōrum est prō patriā morī
phrases.english: it is sweet and fitting to die for one’s country

phrases.latin: Nisi Phaedria haud cessāvit prō tē ēnītī.
phrases.english: Only, Phaedria hasn’t stopped working hard for you.

phrases.latin: solet fierī. — rogāmus mittās. — posteā sī fēcerit, nēmō nostrum prō illō rogābit
phrases.english: It happens. — Please let him off. — If he does it again, none of us will plead for him.

phrases.latin: nec sibi sōlī, sed conjugī, līberīs cēterīsque, quōs cārōs habeat tuērīque dēbeat
phrases.english: (nature makes a man provide) not for himself alone, but for his wife, his children and the others he holds dear and ought to protect
